correctness.rationale: For arbitrary real histories, normalized positive weights imply strict sup-window sine contraction over each block, proving global extinction. For strictly positive histories comparison supplies matching n^{-1/2} bounds. The primitive nonnegative companion matrix has a simple unit eigenvalue and all others strictly interior; standard smooth center manifold and stable tracking apply. Exact inverse-iterate Taylor coefficients give A=-1/(6(1+μ)) and B=(μ+ν)/(24(1+μ)^3)-μ/(12(1+μ)^2)+1/(120(1+μ)); summing the inverse-square increments produces a finite renormalized limit because the remaining O(log n/n²) error is summable. ν≤mμ yields the sharp m=4 cancellation and first negative example at m=5. Exact Fraction arithmetic and 400000-step finite diagnostic checks pass, but infinite conclusions rest on the proof, not experiments.

value.rationale: The first two delay moments control distinct orders of physically meaningful critical relaxation: kernels with identical mean lag and n^{-1/2} decay can have opposite-sign logarithmic corrections. The cutoff m≤3 positive, first cancellation at lag four, first negative at lag five is sharp, parameter-independent, and gives a structural boundary on the smallest memory horizon able to reverse the correction. This exact natural invariant is useful to characterize critical slowing down beyond linear stability and is not a routine restatement of scalar sine iteration.
